source_text:
Ἄσωμεν τὸ ᾆσμα τὸ καινόν, ἰδοὺ γὰρ Ἀδὰμ ἀνεκαινίσθη καὶ Εὔα εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀνεκομίσθη, ὁ γὰρ διάβολος εἰς τὸ
πῦρ ἐσκελίσθη. Χρησώμεθα παρὰ Μαρίας τῆς ἀδελφῆς Μωϋσέως τὸ ᾆσμα ἐκεῖνο, πρέπει γὰρ ἡμῖν νῦν ᾗπερ τότε ἐκείνοις. Συμπαρέστω ἡμῖν καὶ ὁ τῶν ἁγίων ἐκείνων χορὸς καὶ λεγέτω ὃ τότε ἐπὶ τῆς Ἐρυθρᾶς θαλάσσης ἐκελάδιζεν, τό· Ἄσωμεν τῷ κυρίῳ, ἐνδόξως γὰρ δεδόξασται. Τί γὰρ πεποίηκεν; Ἵππον καὶ ἀναβάτην ἔρριψεν εἰς θάλασσαν. Ἵππον καὶ ἀναβάτην· ἵππον μὲν τὴν θηλυμανῆ ἁμαρτίαν, ἀναβάτην δὲ τὸν ἐπὶ τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ καθήμενον δαίμονα ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι τοῦ λουτροῦ κατεπόντισεν. Ἄσωμεν οὖν τῷ κυρίῳ, ἐνδόξως γὰρ δεδόξασται· τὸν γὰρ Φαραὼ καὶ τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ ἔρριψεν εἰς θάλασσαν, τουτέστιν τὸν διάβολον καὶ τὸ σκοτεινὸν καὶ ἐναγὲς τῶν δαιμόνων αὐτοῦ στρατόπεδον ἐν τῷ λουτρῷ τοῦ βαπτίσματος ἐθαλάσσωσεν. Οὐκέτι φοβοῦμαι ἀκούειν· Γῆ εἶ καὶ εἰς γῆν ἀπελεύσῃ· ἐν γὰρ τῷ βαπτίσματι τὴν γῆν ἀπεθέμην καὶ οὐρανὸν ἐνεδυσάμην καὶ ἀκούω· οὐρανὸς εἶ καὶ εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀπελεύσῃ· ὅσοι γὰρ εἰς Χριστὸν ἐβαπτίσθητε Χριστὸν ἐνεδύσασθε, καί· οἷος ὁ χοϊκός, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ χοϊκοί, καὶ οἷος ὁ ἐπουράνιος, τοιοῦτοι καὶ οἱ ἐπουράνιοι. ∆εῖ ἡμᾶς νεφέλαις ἐπιβῆναι καὶ εἰς οὐρανοὺς ἀναδραμεῖν· οὐκ ἀμάρτυρος ὁ λόγος, ἄκουε τοῦ Παύλου λέγοντος· Ἁρπαγησόμεθα ἐν νεφέλαις εἰς ἀπάντησιν τοῦ κυρίου εἰς ἀέρα καὶ οὕτως πάντοτε σὺν κυρίῳ ἐσόμεθα. ∆ιὸ καθὼς ἠκούσαμεν ἀρτίως τοῦ ψαλμῳδοῦ ἡμῖν παραινοῦντος καὶ λέγον τος· Αὕτη ἡ ἡμέρα ἣν ἐποίησεν ὁ κύριος, ἀγαλλιασώμεθα καὶ εὐ φρανθῶμεν ἐν αὐτῇ. Ἀγαλλιασώμεθα οὖν οὐ μέθῃ καὶ κραιπάλῃ σκοτούμενοι, αὕτη γὰρ οὐκ ἂν εἴη εὐφροσύνη ἀλλὰ ἀφροσύνη καὶ σκοτομήνη καρδίας. Ἀγαλλιασώμεθα σκιρτῶντες τῷ πνεύματι, ἀγαλλιασώμεθα ἀγάπῃ ἑστιώμενοι, ἐλπίδι χαίροντες. Εἰ δὲ δεῖ καὶ ἑτέραν ἐννοεῖν εὐφροσύνην καρδίας, τὸν οὐράνιον ἄρτον καθαραῖς παλάμαις ὑποδεξάμενοι τῇ ψυχῇ παραπέμψωμεν ζωῆς αἰωνίου ἐφόδιον ὄντα· καθαραῖς παλάμαις ὑποδεξάμενοι λέγω δέ, οὐχ ὕδατι κοινῷ πεπλυμέναις, ἀλλ' εὐποιΐαις λαμπρυνομέναις. Καὶ τὸ θεῖον καὶ οὐράνιον κρᾶμα ῥοδοείδεσι χείλεσιν ἀρυσώμεθα, οὐ φοίνικί τινι ἐρυθαίνοντες, ἀλλὰ τῷ αἵματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πορφυρίζοντες. Ὦ μεγάλης ὡς ἀληθῶς καὶ ἀγαθῆς ἡμέρας, ἐν ᾗ ὁ ἀμνὸς σφαγιάζεται καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἀγοράζεται καὶ ὁ ποιμὴν ἡμῶν ζῇ· Ἐγὼ γάρ εἰμι, φησίν, ὁ ποιμὴν ὁ καλός. Ὦ μυστηρίου καινοῦ καὶ θαύματος παραδόξου! Σταυρὸς ἔστη καὶ Χριστὸς ἐφηπλώθη καὶ θάνατος ἄδικος ἦν τὸ φαινόμενον καὶ θάλαμος ἅγιος ἦν τὸ γινόμενον, σταυρὸς ἦν τὸ φαινόμενον καὶ παστὸς ἦν τὸ τελούμε νον· χθὲς ἀνέστη παστὸς καὶ σήμερον ἐτέχθη λαός. Ὦ θάνατος Χριστοῦ, θανάτου θάνατος καὶ γλυκεῖαν ζωὴν ἐν τῷ πικροτάτῳ θανάτῳ πηγάζων! Ὦ μυστηρίου Ἀβραμιαίου ἐν Χριστῷ τελουμένου!
thought_title: The New Song of Baptism and the Bridal Chamber of the Cross
orientation: Amphilochius is preaching to the newly baptized, urging them to sing the new song and interpreting the Red Sea victory as a type of baptism.
pass_a_gloss: Let us sing the new song, for behold Adam has been renewed and Eve has been carried up into the heavens, for the devil has been hurled into the fire. Let us borrow from Miriam the sister of Moses that song, for it befits us now just as it befitted them then. Let the chorus of those holy ones be present with us and let it say what it then sang at the Red Sea, namely: Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been gloriously glorified. For what has he done? Horse and rider he has thrown into the sea. Horse and rider: the horse, namely the sin that rages after the female, and the rider, namely the demon sitting upon sin, he sank in the baptism of the washing. Let us sing therefore to the Lord, for he has been gloriously glorified: for Pharaoh and his power he has thrown into the sea, that is, the devil and the dark and accursed camp of his demons he has drowned in the washing of baptism. No longer do I fear to hear: Earth you are and to earth you shall go; for in baptism I have put off the earth and have put on heaven, and I hear: Heaven you are and to the heavens you shall go; for as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ, and: as is the man of dust, so also are those of dust, and as is the heavenly man, so also are those of heaven. We must mount upon clouds and run up into the heavens; the word is not without witness; hear Paul saying: We shall be snatched up in clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so we shall always be with the Lord. Therefore, just as we have just now heard the psalmist urging us and saying: This is the day which the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it. Let us rejoice therefore, not being darkened by drunkenness and debauchery, for this would not be gladness but folly and darkening of heart. Let us rejoice, leaping in the Spirit; let us rejoice, feasting on love, rejoicing in hope. And if we must also consider another gladness of heart, having received the heavenly bread with pure hands let us send it on to the soul as provision for eternal life; having received it with pure hands, I mean, not hands washed with common water, but hands made bright by good deeds. And let us draw the divine and heavenly mixture with rose-colored lips, not reddening them with any crimson dye, but making them purple with the blood of Jesus Christ. O truly great and good day, on which the lamb is slain and the world is purchased and our shepherd lives; for I am, he says, the good shepherd. O new mystery and strange wonder! The cross stood and Christ was stretched out upon it, and death was unjust as to what appeared, and a holy bridal chamber was what was coming to be; the cross was what appeared and a bridal chamber was what was being accomplished; yesterday the bridal chamber was set up and today a people was born. O death of Christ, death of death and welling up sweet life in the most bitter death! O mystery of Abraham being accomplished in Christ!

choices.why: The verb is passive; the devil is the object of divine action, not the agent of his own stumbling.

choices.english: the sin that rages after the female
choices.why: The compound adjective describes sin's lustful, woman-mad character; the rendering keeps the compound's force without a hyphenated English compound.
The verb is coined from θάλασσα (sea) and means to make into sea, to drown; the rendering preserves the sea imagery tied to baptism.

choices.english: the bridal chamber was set up
choices.why: ἀνέστη here means 'was erected, was set up,' not 'arose' in the resurrection sense; the bridal chamber is established, not resurrected.
The verb means to spread or stretch out upon something; it describes Christ's body being spread upon the cross.
The term denotes the nuptial chamber; the homily uses it as a figure for the cross as the place of Christ's union with his people.

pass_b_english: Let us sing the new song, for behold, Adam has been renewed and Eve has been carried up to the heavens, for the devil has been hurled into the fire. Let us borrow that song from Miriam, the sister of Moses, for it suits us now just as it suited them then. Let the chorus of those holy ones stand with us and sing what it sang then at the Red Sea: “Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously glorified” (Exodus 15:1). For what has he done? “Horse and rider he has thrown into the sea” (Exodus 15:1). Horse and rider: the horse is the sin that is mad for women, and the rider is the demon seated upon sin, and in the baptismal washing he drowned them both. Let us sing then to the Lord, for he is gloriously glorified, for he has thrown Pharaoh and his power into the sea (Exodus 15:4)—that is, in the baptismal washing he has drowned in the sea the devil and the dark and accursed camp of his demons. I no longer fear to hear: “Earth you are, and to earth you shall return” (Genesis 3:19). For in baptism I put off the earth and put on heaven, and I hear: Heaven you are, and to the heavens you shall return. For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ (Galatians 3:27), and: As is the man of dust, so are those who are of dust; and as is the man of heaven, so are those who are of heaven (1 Corinthians 15:48). We must mount upon the clouds and run up to the heavens. The word is not without witness; hear Paul saying: We shall be snatched up in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so we shall always be with the Lord (1 Thessalonians 4:17). Therefore, as we have just heard the psalmist urging us and saying: This is the day the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it (Psalm 118:24 (LXX 117:24)), let us rejoice then, not darkened by drunkenness and dissipation, for that would not be gladness but foolishness and darkness of heart. Let us rejoice, leaping in the Spirit; let us rejoice, entertained by love, rejoicing in hope. And if we must consider another gladness of heart, let us receive the heavenly bread with pure hands and send it on to the soul as provision for eternal life—with pure hands, I say, not washed with common water but made bright by good deeds. And let us draw the divine and heavenly mixture with rose-colored lips, reddening them not with some purple dye but making them crimson with the blood of Jesus Christ. O what a truly great and good day, on which the lamb is slain and the world is purchased and our shepherd lives! For I am, he says, the good shepherd (John 10:11). O new mystery and strange wonder! The cross stood and Christ was stretched out upon it, and what appeared was an unjust death, but what was happening was a holy bridal chamber; what appeared was a cross, but what was being accomplished was a bridal chamber. Yesterday the bridal chamber arose, and today a people was born. O death of Christ, death of death, pouring forth sweet life in the bitterest death! O Abrahamic mystery being fulfilled in Christ!

problems.quote: the sin that rages after the female
problems.why: θηλυμανής means 'mad after women/lustful', not 'rages after the female'
problems.fix: the sin that is mad for women, or lustful sin

problems.quote: Yesterday the bridal chamber was set up
problems.why: ἀνέστη means 'rose/arose', not 'was set up'; bridal chamber 'rose' (resurrection)
Ἀβραμιαῖος is adjective 'Abrahamic', not 'Abraham being'; genitive of mystery
problems.fix: O Abrahamic mystery being fulfilled in Christ!
problems.ruling: Ἀβραμιαῖου is adjective 'Abrahamic' modifying μυστηρίου; 'Abraham being fulfilled' misreads syntax.

fixed: θηλυμανῆ means 'mad after women/lustful', so 'rages after the female' misstates it; changed to 'mad for women'.
ἀνέστη means 'arose/rose', not 'was set up'; changed to 'arose'.
Ἀβραμιαῖος is the adjective 'Abrahamic', not 'Abraham being'; changed to 'Abrahamic mystery'.

problems.why: ἀνέστη means 'rose, stood up, arose'—but with παστός (bridal chamber) it means the bridal chamber 'was set up/established,' not 'arose' as in resurrection. The English suggests the bridal chamber itself rose from death.
problems.fix: the bridal chamber was made ready
problems.ruling: ἀνέστη παστός: ἀνέστη here means 'arose/rose' (resurrection context); 'arose' is correct, not 'was set up.'

edits.new: Yesterday the bridal chamber was set up

fixed: Changed 'arose' to 'was set up' because ἀνέστη with παστός means the bridal chamber was established or set up, not that it rose from death.

problems.quote: Yesterday the bridal chamber was set up, and today a people was born.
problems.source_quote: χθὲς ἀνέστη παστὸς καὶ σήμερον ἐτέχθη λαός
problems.why: Source says 'yesterday the bridal chamber rose/arose'; English says 'was set up,' losing the resurrection echo of ἀνέστη.
problems.fix: Yesterday the bridal chamber arose, and today a people was born.
problems.ruling: ἀνέστη means 'rose/arose,' with clear resurrection echo; 'was set up' loses this meaning.

problems.why: σκοτομήνη is 'darkness' (noun), not 'darkened' (participle/adjective)—the Greek has 'darkness of heart' or 'heart's darkness', a noun phrase in apposition. The English 'a darkened heart' makes it an adjectival description, changing the grammar. The Greek means 'foolishness and darkness of heart'—two nouns in apposition to the preceding.
problems.ruling: σκοτομήνη is a noun ('darkness'), not adjective; 'darkness of heart' needed, not 'a darkened heart'.

problems.why: ἑστιώμενοι is passive 'being feasted, entertained as guests'—the English 'feasting on love' makes love the object of feasting (we feast on love), but the Greek means 'being feasted with love' or 'entertained by love' (love is the host, not the food). The agency is reversed: in Greek, love feasts us; in English, we feast on love.
problems.ruling: ἑστιώμενοι is passive 'being feasted'; love is host not food. 'Feasting on love' reverses agency.

edits.old: Yesterday the bridal chamber was set up, and today a people was born.
edits.new: Yesterday the bridal chamber arose, and today a people was born.

fixed: Omission: 'was set up' loses the resurrection echo of ἀνέστη; changed to 'arose'.
Mistranslation: σκοτομήνη is a noun 'darkness', not an adjective; changed to 'darkness of heart'.
Mistranslation: ἑστιώμενοι is passive 'being feasted/entertained'; changed to 'entertained by love'.

dismissed.why: σφαγιάζεται means 'is slain as a sacrifice, is immolated'—the English 'slain' loses the sacrificial nuance. However, 'lamb is slain' with context carries sacrificial meaning. This is borderline. Withdrawing as within range.
dismissed.note: The checker withdrew this itself, and "the lamb is slain" is a fair rendering of σφαγιάζεται.
